scenario: Personal data field ('email') nested one level inside an innocuous-looking parent key ('contact')
expected: Reject — INV-ZA-1 applies to Zone A content regardless of nesting depth

actual.errorMessage: Zone A write rejected: field 'contact.email' resembles personal data (INV-ZA-1, SOV §Zone A)

classification: Fixed — was a real gap (Type I, our own code)
note: Prior to this fix, assertNoPersonalData() only scanned top-level keys of the Zone A object, so { contact: { email: '...' } } passed silently — the denylist check never saw the 'email' key because it only ever inspected 'contact'. Fixed by recursing into nested plain objects (arrays intentionally left unrecursed for this pass — see SDB-03). This was a correctness bug in our own implementation of a stated MUST (INV-ZA-1), not a draft ambiguity, so fixed directly rather than merely logged.
